item.title: Ransomware Exploits VMware vCenter CVE-2026-59310 as Vite and Marimo Attacks Expand
item.content:encoded:
Window: 15 Sep 10:00 → 15 Sep 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

CISA: Critical VMware RCE flaw now exploited by ransomware gangs — Must Read

CISA says ransomware groups are now exploiting the critical VMware vCenter Syslog Server directory-traversal RCE flaw CVE-2026-59310, which was patched in July and added to the KEV catalog. Organizations should urgently patch exposed vCenter systems, as attackers have already used the flaw to establish reverse SSH access.

  • CISA has flagged CVE-2026-59310, a critical VMware vCenter Syslog Server flaw patched by Broadcom on July 29, as actively used in ransomware campaigns.
  • The flaw is a directory-traversal issue that unauthenticated attackers can use to run arbitrary code on affected vCenter systems.
  • QUIRSO reported that a suspected advanced persistent threat actor compromised more than 361 IP addresses in 47 countries and deployed a reverse SSH tool after exploiting the flaw.
  • CISA added CVE-2026-59310 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog and required U.S. government agencies to secure affected vCenter systems within three days.
  • Shadowserver tracks more than 450 VMware vCenter servers exposed to the internet, though the number patched against this flaw is unknown.

Technologies: hypervisor, remote-access

Products: vmware-vcenter-server, vmware-vcenter-syslog-server, vmware-esxi

Vendors: broadcom, vmware

Human Attacker Exploits Marimo RCE, Reaches SSH Bastion in Eight Seconds — Should Read

Sysdig observed a skilled attacker exploit the critical Marimo RCE flaw CVE-2026-39987 and pivot to an SSH bastion using AWS Secrets Manager credentials in just eight seconds, demonstrating that human operators can match AI-assisted attack speed while evading common traps.

  • Sysdig reported that a threat actor exploited CVE-2026-39987, a pre-authentication remote-code-execution flaw affecting all versions of Marimo, to gain an interactive shell.
  • After gaining access, the operator used credentials harvested from the compromised instance to call AWS Secrets Manager, retrieve an SSH private key, and authenticate to a bastion host in eight seconds.
  • Sysdig said the attacker ran more than 850 interactive commands during a nine-hour session and used hand-written scripts rather than recognizable public offensive tools or an AI agent.
  • Hunt.io identified a cryptomining campaign compromising 3,562 Redis servers, with rogue Redis replication used to deploy an XMRig miner.
  • Hunt.io said the Redis victims ranged from Redis 2.8.17 through 7.2.0 and that missing authentication, rather than a version-specific flaw, appeared to be the primary weakness.

Technologies: secrets-manager, cloud-platform, database, cms, iot-device

Products: marimo, aws-secrets-manager, redis, wordpress, mongodb, dahua-ip-cameras, xmrig

Vendors: sysdig, hunt-io, marimo, amazon-web-services, redis, automattic, mongodb, dahua-technology

Mass-Scanning Campaign Exploits Vite Flaw to Extract Cloud Credentials From Exposed Dev Servers — Should Read

Attackers are mass-scanning internet-exposed Vite development servers to exploit CVE-2026-39364, bypassing file-deny rules with query parameters to steal .env files, cloud credentials, and infrastructure configuration data. Organizations should patch Vite and ensure development servers are not publicly exposed.

  • F5 Labs observed an automated campaign in August 2026 that scanned internet-exposed Vite development servers to steal cloud credentials, configuration files, and infrastructure state files.
  • The campaign exploits CVE-2026-39364, a Vite flaw with a CVSS score of 8.2 that can allow unauthenticated requests with query parameters such as ?raw or ?import&raw to retrieve files blocked by server.fs.deny.
  • An application is affected when its Vite development server is exposed to a network, the sensitive file is within directories allowed by server.fs.allow, and the file matches a server.fs.deny rule.
  • Observed requests targeted environment files, AWS credentials and configurations, Terraform state files, Azure profiles, and system paths including /etc/passwd and /proc/self/cwd/.env.
  • The malicious requests used spoofed crawler and AI-bot User-Agent headers and forged X-Forwarded-For and X-Real-IP values, with significant activity originating from the United States, Belgium, the Netherlands, Singapore, and Taiwan.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: vite, amazon-web-services, microsoft-azure, google-cloud-platform

Vendors: vite, f5, amazon-web-services, microsoft, google

ParaShells: Parallels Desktop Turns Appliance Install Into a Root Shell — Should Read

JFrog researchers found that Parallels Desktop 26.4.0 can let any low-privileged local macOS user gain root by abusing its world-writable privileged service socket and an argument-injection flaw in appliance extraction. The issue, tracked as CVE-2026-90894, was fixed in Parallels Desktop 27.0.0.

  • JFrog researchers found that Parallels Desktop 26.4.0 build 57513 on Apple silicon allowed a non-administrator local user to execute code as root through the prl_disp_service helper.
  • The attack uses the world-writable /var/run/prl_disp_service.socket, where an unsigned local client can successfully use PrlSrv_LoginLocal without Parallels code signing.
  • A quote in the appliance installation parent path can inject a tar option that causes macOS tar to run an attacker-controlled program with root privileges.
  • The issue is tracked as CVE-2026-90894 and was fixed in Parallels Desktop 27.0.0.
  • The article states that a running virtual machine is not required for the proven attack path, provided the privileged helper and its socket are present.

Technologies: hypervisor, operating-system

Products: parallels-desktop, prl-disp-service, macos

Vendors: parallels, apple, jfrog

Have it both ways: stay discoverable in search while disallowing AI training — May Read

Cloudflare launched a Disallow AI Training control that lets site owners block AI model training while preserving search indexing for accountable mixed-use crawlers such as Googlebot, Applebot, and Bingbot. The setting publishes no-training preferences through robots.txt and expands Cloudflare’s bot controls across search, training, and agent behavior.

  • Cloudflare introduced a Disallow AI Training setting that publishes a no-training preference in robots.txt while allowing accountable mixed-use crawlers to continue indexing sites for search.
  • Under the new controls, selecting Block or Block on pages with ads applies to mixed-use crawlers such as Applebot, Bingbot, and Googlebot and can therefore affect search discoverability.
  • Apple, Google, and Microsoft are designated Accountable because they provide or have committed to provide controls for AI training and AI summaries, transparency, and assurance that training opt-outs do not affect traditional search results.
  • Cloudflare states that training-only crawlers operated by Amazon, Anthropic, Meta, and OpenAI can be blocked without affecting search because those organizations separate search and training crawlers.
  • Cloudflare plans to develop controls by early next year that let site owners manage how much of their content is included in AI summaries through a single Cloudflare setting.

Technologies: waf, cloud-platform

Products: cloudflare-bot-management, ai-crawl-control, bot-preference-sync, cloudflare-radar, applebot, googlebot, bingbot

Vendors: cloudflare, apple, google, microsoft, amazon, anthropic, meta, openai

Manhattan DA takes down 12 AI deepfake porn sites — May Read

The Manhattan District Attorney’s Office seized 12 domains hosting AI-generated non-consensual pornography involving more than 1,200 people, and says its investigation remains ongoing. Prosecutors warned that deepfake abuse can facilitate harassment and domestic violence, and will monitor for replacement domains.

  • The Manhattan District Attorney’s Office seized the domains of 12 AI deepfake pornography websites for allegedly violating laws on disseminating non-consensual videos.
  • The sites hosted AI-generated videos involving more than 1,200 people and allowed users to use real people’s faces and bodies to create pornography.
  • District Attorney Alvin Bragg said the office knows of domestic violence cases in which partners threatened to release deepfake images of victims.
  • Bragg said the investigation is ongoing and that his office will monitor for attempts to revive the platforms under new domains.
  • Microsoft sued six developers last year over alleged use of Azure OpenAI services to create non-consensual intimate images and sexually explicit content.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: azure-openai, grok

Vendors: microsoft, x

The Renewal Notice for a Domain That Could Not Be Renewed — May Read

A phishing email impersonating Squarespace used a real but dormant company domain to create urgency, yet public registration data showed the domain was already renewed, held by a different registrar, and registry-locked against renewal. The key lesson is to verify domain expiry, registrar, and status codes independently before acting on renewal notices.

  • In late August 2026, a shared partnerships mailbox at a global digital advertising agency received a Squarespace-branded domain renewal email seeking $12.47 for a legacy domain.
  • Public registration data showed that the named domain had been renewed months earlier, was paid through the following year, and was registered with a registrar unrelated to Squarespace.
  • The domain had registry status locks including clientRenewProhibited, meaning the registry would reject any attempt to renew it until the lock was removed.
  • The email authenticated through SPF, DKIM, and DMARC for the attacker-controlled sending domain, while impersonating Squarespace through a display name, organization header, postal addresses, and a branded destination domain.
  • The sole Renew Domain link used a Google shortlink that resolved to a malicious Cloudflare-fronted squarespace.one destination, whose content was not observed because the attacker’s bot protection blocked the scanner.

Technologies: email-security, cloud-platform

Products: squarespace-domains, google-workspace, adaptive-ai, exim

Vendors: squarespace, google, cloudflare, ironscales, gname, exim

China spy chief points at US AI models in cyber threat warning — May Read

China’s intelligence chief warned that U.S. AI models Anthropic Claude Mythos and OpenAI GPT-5.5-Cyber could accelerate vulnerability discovery and malware development, posing risks to China’s critical infrastructure, without alleging either had been used against China.

  • Chen Yixin, head of China’s Ministry of State Security, named Anthropic’s Claude Mythos and OpenAI’s GPT-5.5-Cyber as examples of AI models that could accelerate vulnerability discovery and malware development.
  • Chen did not accuse either U.S. AI model of having been used in attacks on China.
  • Chen said generative AI could be used to fabricate political rumors, spread harmful information, and incite confrontational sentiment at low cost and large scale.
  • Anthropic reported days earlier that a Chinese-speaking group used Claude in what the company described as an autonomous vulnerability research program that found several zero-day flaws in a major security product.
  • China’s Cyberspace Administration released updated AI-governance guidance focused on autonomous agents and embodied AI, identifying loss of control as a core risk.

Products: claude-mythos, gpt-5-5-cyber

Vendors: anthropic, openai

1Password's AI patching benchmark is misleading — May Read

Trail of Bits argues that 1Password’s 26% AI clean-patch headline is misleading because it combines unusually difficult bugs, deliberately wrong instructions, and trials where agents could not test fixes. Its reanalysis found agents blocked the supplied exploit in 86% of reasonably configured trials, while emphasizing that both AI and human fixes require rigorous validation and review.

  • Trail of Bits argues that 1Password’s reported 26% clean-fix rate combines deliberately incorrect repair instructions and trials in which agents could not build or test their patches.
  • After excluding trials that prohibited testing, instructed agents to apply the wrong fix, or consulted the upstream fix, Trail of Bits found that 2,634 of 3,067 generated patches, or 86%, blocked the supplied exploit.
  • Trail of Bits’ review of 2,265 first fixes submitted by developers across 236 security assessments found that 283 first fixes, or 12.5%, did not fully resolve the reported issue.
  • Of 186 closed or merged Patch the Planet pull requests examined by September 14, 2026, maintainers merged 126, and accepted the originally proposed security fix in 91 of those merged pull requests.
  • Trail of Bits released post-patch-validation and review-walkthrough skills to help agents test security fixes and help engineers review code changes.

Technologies: message-queue, operating-system, browser, web-server

Products: flawed, patch-the-planet, post-patch-validation, review-walkthrough, gpt-5-5, opus-4-8, activemq, linux, chromium, freenginx, go-jose, noble-curves

Vendors: 1password, trail-of-bits, openai, anthropic, apache, chromium-project, freenginx, go-jose, paulmillr

Australia is replacing the Essential Eight with a new cyber framework. Here’s how exposure management can help you get ahead of it. — Optional

Australia’s ASD is replacing the Essential Eight with an outcomes-based Essentials series that will require organizations to demonstrate their security posture continuously across enterprise IT, cloud, identity, and OT. The article argues that continuous exposure management can help organizations prioritize and evidence current cyber risks rather than rely on periodic compliance snapshots.

  • The Australian Signals Directorate announced in June 2026 that it will replace the Essential Eight with an outcomes-focused Essentials series, with deprecation targeted to begin around mid-2027 and full retirement around mid-2028.
  • The Essential Eight was designed for on-premises enterprise IT and assessed eight named controls at periodic maturity levels, while the new Essentials series is intended to cover enterprise IT, identity, SaaS, cloud, and operational technology.
  • The first Essentials chapter, covering enterprise IT, reached public consultation in July 2026, while timelines for cloud, operational technology, and potential agentic AI chapters have not been set.
  • The article argues that periodic compliance reports can become outdated quickly in environments where cloud services, identities, SaaS applications, and connected operational technology change frequently.
  • Tenable states that its Tenable One Exposure Management Platform can combine exposure information across multiple environments to help organizations identify critical risks, attack paths, and changes in security posture.

Technologies: cloud-platform, iam

Products: tenable-one, essential-eight, essentials-series, microsoft-365, google-workspace

Vendors: tenable, australian-signals-directorate, microsoft, google

Give every teammate and agent the right level of access to your Workers — Optional

Cloudflare has launched resource-level access controls for Workers, allowing teams and agents to receive narrowly scoped roles for a specific Worker rather than broad account-wide permissions. The new roles support least-privilege debugging, code review, deployment, and administration, with similar controls planned for D1, R2, and KV.

  • Cloudflare has introduced Worker-level access controls that let customers give a user or API token access to a specific Worker rather than to all account resources.
  • The four new roles are Metadata Read-Only, Content Read-Only, Editor, and Admin, and they can be assigned at the Developer Platform, product, or individual resource scope.
  • Metadata Read-Only permits access to Worker settings, metrics, logs, traces, and analytics without exposing source code, while Content Read-Only permits code review without modification or deployment.
  • An Editor token scoped to one Worker can deploy changes to that Worker but cannot delete it or modify other Workers, helping limit the impact of a misconfigured or exposed CI/CD token.
  • Changing a Worker route or Custom Domain requires both Editor access to the Worker and Workers Routes permission for the relevant zone.

Technologies: cloud-platform, database, object-storage, ci-cd, iam

Products: cloudflare-workers, durable-objects, cloudflare-d1, cloudflare-r2, cloudflare-kv, wrangler, terraform

Vendors: cloudflare, hashicorp

Introducing Varonis Data Lifecycle Management — Optional

Varonis launched Data Lifecycle Management, a capability that identifies redundant, obsolete, and trivial data across connected environments and automatically quarantines it using data sensitivity, permissions, activity, and retention context. The company positions it as a way to reduce storage costs, compliance exposure, and AI quality issues without irreversible deletion.

  • Varonis introduced Data Lifecycle Management, a capability designed to automatically find and quarantine redundant, obsolete, and trivial data across an organization’s data estate.
  • The article states that at least 30% of enterprise data is redundant, obsolete, or trivial, contributing to storage costs, degraded AI results, and increased exposure of sensitive information.
  • Varonis Data Lifecycle Management is built on the Varonis Data Security Platform and uses information about data sensitivity, permissions, and activity to identify data that is stale, duplicated, overexposed, or past its retention window.
  • The product provides a unified dashboard for viewing redundant, obsolete, and trivial data, including duplicate clusters, stale files and folders, and data past its retention window.
  • When data violates configured policies for duplicates, staleness, or retention, Varonis automatically moves it to a secure quarantine, and the action can be reversed before deletion.

Technologies: dlp

Products: varonis-data-lifecycle-management, varonis-data-security-platform

Vendors: varonis

What Zero-Day Response Should Be in the Post-Mythos Era — Optional

Sponsored by Picus Security, the article argues that organizations should validate likely attack techniques and compensating controls immediately after a zero-day disclosure rather than wait for a patch or public exploit. It promotes combining exploitability validation, breach-and-attack simulation, and controlled real-exploit testing to close exposure gaps at machine speed.

  • PaperCut said on August 27 that attackers were already exploiting PaperCut NG and MF servers before a CVE, public exploit, or patch was available, and its third emergency patch was released September 1.
  • The article argues that organizations can test the likely steps of an attack, such as delivery, execution, privilege escalation, process injection, and credential access, even when no working exploit is publicly available.
  • In the article's hypothetical scenario, security-control testing identified missed delivery, non-blocking web-application firewall detection, and absent endpoint and SIEM alerts, then prompted rules and hardening changes.
  • After threat intelligence linked the hypothetical CVE-2026-1001 to an Iranian group, a wider attack simulation found a missed persistence technique that was subsequently addressed.
  • The sponsored article promotes using exploitability validation, security-control validation, and agentic pentesting together to respond to zero-day vulnerabilities before patches are available.

Technologies: firewall, waf, edr, siem

Products: picus-platform, papercut-ng, papercut-mf

Vendors: picus-security, papercut

Attack Chains, Not Just Attack Surfaces: Why Testing Individual Techniques Misses the Point — Optional

Filigran argues that security validation should test end-to-end attack chains rather than isolated techniques, since attackers combine phishing, credential abuse, lateral movement, and exfiltration to exploit gaps between controls. Its OpenAEV platform promotes automated, conditional attack-chain simulations—including AI-assisted autonomous execution—to continuously identify the chokepoints that would stop a real intrusion.

  • The article argues that testing individual security techniques does not show whether a real attacker could combine multiple steps into a successful intrusion.
  • Filigran's State of Threat Management report is cited as finding that 93% of security leaders reported a business-impacting cyberattack in the prior 12 months, while 84% cited siloed tools and disconnected testing as a reason exposures go unnoticed.
  • The article describes Attack Chaining in Filigran OpenAEV as a way to automate multi-stage attack simulations in which the results of one step determine the next step.
  • OpenAEV attack chains can use defined boundaries for assets, targets, permitted actions, and escalation limits, according to the article.
  • The article says XTM One can enable an AI agent to plan, execute, and adapt an attack chain from an operator-defined objective and scope.

Technologies: orchestration

Products: openaev, xtm-one

Vendors: filigran

The Defensible AI-SOC: SOC Modernization for the Mythos Era | Corelight — Optional

Corelight promotes a “defensible AI-SOC” approach to SOC modernization, emphasizing the need for trustworthy, explainable security operations as AI-driven threats and tooling evolve.

  • The article is titled “The Defensible AI-SOC: SOC Modernization for the Mythos Era.”
  • The article concerns modernization of security operations centers, or SOCs.
  • The article presents the concept of a “defensible AI-SOC.”
  • Corelight is identified as the article’s publisher.

Technologies: network-monitoring

Vendors: corelight

item.title: Actively Exploited Cisco Secure Email Gateway CVE-2026-76461 Drives Urgent Patching
item.content:encoded:
Window: 15 Sep 06:00 → 15 Sep 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

Cisco patches Secure Email Gateway zero-day exploited in attacks — Must Read

Cisco has patched CVE-2026-76461, a critical zero-day in Secure Email Gateway email parsing that is actively exploited to execute root-level commands remotely. Organizations should apply updates immediately and review mail, network, and firewall logs for signs of malicious SQL statements or suspicious external transfers.

  • Cisco patched CVE-2026-76461, a critical Cisco Secure Email Gateway zero-day that it says threat actors have actively exploited since at least September 2026.
  • The flaw affects Cisco AsyncOS Software on physical and virtual Secure Email Gateway appliances regardless of configuration and can let an unauthenticated remote attacker execute commands with root privileges.
  • Cisco said the issue stems from insufficient validation in email parsing, allowing a crafted email containing malicious SQL statements to trigger arbitrary SQL execution and operating-system command execution.
  • Cisco provided indicators of compromise and advised administrators to inspect mail_logs for suspicious SQL statements and review network and firewall logs for suspicious transfers to or from external or malicious IP addresses.
  • CISA added CVE-2026-76461 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog and directed U.S. federal agencies to patch affected systems by September 17.

Technologies: email-security, firewall

Products: cisco-secure-email-gateway, cisco-asyncos, cisco-secure-email-and-web-manager, cisco-secure-firewall-management-center

Vendors: cisco

LiteSpeed Enterprise Flaw Could Let One Hosting Account Gain Root Access on a Shared Server — Must Read

LiteSpeed Web Server Enterprise versions before 6.3.7 contain a critical flaw that could allow a low-privilege shared-hosting account to gain root access and bypass account isolation controls. Administrators should manually update to version 6.3.7 immediately, as auto-update availability may be delayed.

  • LiteSpeed Web Server Enterprise versions before 6.3.7 contain a critical flaw that could allow a low-privilege shared-hosting account to gain root access on the server.
  • cPanel warned that the issue can bypass account-separation controls, including CloudLinux CageFS, potentially allowing access to or alteration of other hosted sites and server files.
  • LiteSpeed released version 6.3.7 on September 11, and cPanel advised administrators to install it using /usr/local/lsws/admin/misc/lsup.sh -f -v 6.3.7.
  • Neither cPanel nor LiteSpeed publicly described the flaw’s mechanism, assigned it a CVE identifier or severity score, or provided indicators of compromise or a workaround.
  • LiteSpeed said automatic delivery of version 6.3.7 may be delayed, while its download page still listed version 6.3.6 as the stable release as of September 15.

Technologies: web-server

Products: litespeed-web-server-enterprise, litespeed-cpanel-plugin, openlitespeed, cagefs

Vendors: litespeed-technologies, cpanel, cloudlinux

Suspected Black Axe gang leaders face cybercrime charges in the US — Should Read

Five alleged Black Axe leaders were extradited from South Africa to the United States to face wire fraud, money laundering, and identity theft charges over a decade-long romance-scam and advance-fee fraud operation.

  • Five alleged leaders of the Black Axe cybercrime syndicate were extradited from South Africa to the United States to face wire fraud and money laundering charges.
  • Prosecutors allege that the defendants coordinated advance-fee and romance fraud schemes from Cape Town between 2011 and 2021.
  • The alleged scheme used aliases, social media, dating websites, and internet-based phone numbers to persuade U.S. victims to send money.
  • The defendants were arrested in South Africa in 2021 at the United States' request and extradited on September 11, 2026.
  • If convicted, they face up to 20 years for wire fraud, up to 20 years for money laundering, and an additional two years for aggravated identity theft.

Microsoft confirms KB5002914 Excel update breaks copy and paste — Should Read

Microsoft confirmed that the September 2026 KB5002914 Office security update can silently break copy, paste, autofill, and formula dragging in Excel versions 2016 through 2024. Microsoft is investigating, while affected users report that uninstalling or rolling back the update restores functionality.

  • Microsoft confirmed that the September 2026 KB5002914 security update can cause copy and paste to silently fail in Excel.
  • The issue affects Microsoft Excel 2016, 2019, 2021, and 2024, and reports also cite problems with autofill and formula dragging.
  • When the failure occurs, the copied source remains selected while the target location is unchanged, with no beep or error message shown to the user.
  • Microsoft is investigating the issue and says it will provide more information in its support article when available.
  • Affected users have reported that uninstalling KB5002914 or rolling back to specified earlier Office versions restores copy-and-paste functionality.

Technologies: operating-system, cloud-platform, remote-access, hypervisor

Products: microsoft-excel, office-2016, office-2019, office-2021, office-2024, windows-11, windows-365, remote-desktop-services, hyper-v

Vendors: microsoft

item.title: Netskope Calls for Enterprise Kill Switches and Real-Time AI Agent Controls
item.content:encoded:
Window: 14 Sep 22:00 → 15 Sep 02:00 UTC (4 hours)

Trying to Pace the Frontier is Not Going to Secure the Enterprise — Optional

Enterprise AI security cannot wait for frontier-model pacing or regulation: organizations need real-time controls over agent identity, network access, and data, plus an immediate enterprise-controlled kill switch. The article argues that inline inspection and collaboration between AI labs and security vendors are essential to contain AI-agent misuse and adversarial abuse.

  • The article argues that enterprises cannot depend on international agreements or frontier AI labs slowing development to address risks from AI systems already being deployed inside companies.
  • Employees and developers may connect AI agents and copilots to customer, finance, and other business systems without adequate limits, creating opportunities for data exposure and unauthorized access.
  • The author says an enterprise-controlled kill switch should let a company immediately stop an AI agent by revoking its identity, cutting its network access, freezing its data access, or all three.
  • The article advocates inspecting AI-agent actions against applications in real time to stop agents that move beyond their assigned tasks.
  • The author cites Anthropic’s Project Glasswing as an example of frontier AI capabilities being shared under controls with security companies to identify and fix software flaws before adversaries can exploit them.

Technologies: casb, dlp

Products: netskope-one, project-glasswing

Vendors: netskope, anthropic, openai, alphabet, hugging-face

item.title: VPN Breaches, OAuth Token Exposure, and ClickFix Malware Abuse
item.content:encoded:
Window: 14 Sep 18:00 → 14 Sep 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

Microsoft releases emergency Windows updates to fix RDS failures — Should Read

Microsoft released emergency out-of-band Windows updates to fix Remote Desktop Services failures caused by September 2026 security updates across affected Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server systems. The updates also address certain Hyper-V shared-folder and multichannel USB audio issues, though some USB Audio Class 1.0 problems remain unresolved.

  • Microsoft released emergency out-of-band Windows updates on September 14 to address Remote Desktop Services failures caused by September security updates.
  • Affected systems experienced Remote Desktop connection and sign-in failures, and some servers became unresponsive; related tools such as Microsoft Management Console, File Explorer, and Windows Update could also stop responding.
  • The updates include KB5129236 for Windows 10 21H2 and 22H2, KB5129195 for Windows 11 24H2 and 25H2, KB5129194 for Windows 11 26H1, and separate updates for Windows Server 2019, 2022, and 2025.
  • The Windows 11 out-of-band updates also fix a Hyper-V folder-sharing issue involving Linux virtual machines and certain multichannel USB audio failures.
  • Microsoft says some USB Audio Class 1.0 devices may still fail to start or produce audio after the September 8 security update, and it is working on a further fix.

Technologies: operating-system, remote-access, hypervisor

Products: windows-10, windows-11, windows-server-2019, windows-server-2022, windows-server-2025, remote-desktop-services, hyper-v, host-compute-service

Vendors: microsoft

Hackers hijack HBO Max Reddit account to push malware in ClickFix ads — Should Read

Hackers hijacked HBO Max’s verified Reddit account to run more than 100 malicious ads that used ClickFix social engineering to trick Windows and macOS users into installing information-stealing malware. The campaign, linked to PasteSwitch, also promoted fake AI, developer, and cryptocurrency-wallet software.

  • Hackers compromised HBO Max’s verified u/hbomax Reddit account and used it to launch 108 malicious advertisements over roughly 48 hours.
  • The ads used ClickFix instructions that persuaded visitors to copy and paste commands into Windows Run, PowerShell, or macOS Terminal instead of downloading legitimate software.
  • Researchers at Hudson Rock and ADAMnetworks linked the activity to the PasteSwitch campaign, which has distributed information stealers, loaders, cryptocurrency clippers, and fake cryptocurrency wallet applications.
  • One fake HBO Max site directed macOS users to run a command that downloaded and executed a script from attacker-controlled infrastructure.
  • Researchers identified ads directing users to fake HBO Max, AI/developer software, macOS utility, and code-desktop websites, and Reddit paused the ads after they were reported.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: reddit, windows, macos, powershell, microsoft-amsi

Vendors: reddit, microsoft, apple

3BB Attacker Used MeshCentral Backdoor for Root Access, Targeted Subscriber Credentials — Should Read

Hunt.io found evidence that an attacker had root-level access inside Thai broadband provider 3BB and used a covert MeshCentral deployment to maintain control while targeting subscriber RADIUS credentials. The intrusion may have involved an unpatched FortiGate SSL-VPN vulnerable to CVE-2024-21762, but the initial access method and any data theft remain unconfirmed.

  • Hunt.io captured an exposed attacker server on June 3, 2026, and found evidence that the attacker had obtained root-level access to internal systems at Thai broadband provider 3BB.
  • The attacker configured MeshCentral as a concealed remote-access backdoor, with agents reporting to www.ayuthayatech[.]com in a device group named TH-3BB.
  • Recovered scripts targeted more than 55 internal computers with SSH password spraying, searched for stored credentials and SSH keys, and could install web shells and additional SSH keys.
  • The toolkit included scripts designed to copy 3BB RADIUS databases containing subscriber login credentials, although Hunt.io found evidence of targeting rather than confirmed data theft.
  • The attacker also had tooling for CVE-2024-21762 against a vulnerable 3BB FortiGate SSL-VPN gateway, but Hunt.io could not confirm that this flaw was used for initial access.

Technologies: remote-access, firewall, vpn

Products: meshcentral, fortigate, fortios

Vendors: fortinet

Japan's Digital Agency says VPN flaw exposed 246,000 personnel records — Should Read

Japan’s Digital Agency says attackers exploited a known, medium-severity VPN flaw to access a government system, potentially exposing roughly 246,000 personnel-data records. The agency contained the intrusion and reports no confirmed misuse or impact on public-facing government services.

  • Japan’s Digital Agency said an attacker exploited a known, medium-severity flaw in a VPN device used by the Government Solution Service to gain unauthorized system access.
  • The agency’s investigation began on June 25 after it detected large-scale file access from a maintenance and operations staff member’s account, and it identified the unauthorized access on July 9.
  • Potentially exposed information included about 236,000 names, 231,000 email addresses, 94,000 telephone numbers, and 1,000 physical addresses.
  • The affected people include government employees, public officials, and associated businesses and individuals using the Government Solution Service, while the agency said general-public data, My Number identifiers, bank details, and pension numbers were not exposed.
  • The agency reported no detected misuse of the information, contained the incident on July 9, and said government service availability was not affected.

Technologies: vpn, remote-access

Products: government-solution-service

Vendors: digital-agency

Members of ‘Black Axe’ cybercriminal group extradited from South Africa — Should Read

Five alleged Black Axe leaders were extradited from South Africa to the United States to face wire fraud and money laundering charges tied to decade-long romance scams that targeted more than 100 victims.

  • Five alleged members of the Black Axe cybercriminal organization were extradited from South Africa and are scheduled to appear in U.S. District Court in Trenton, New Jersey.

Twitch extension with 30K installs exposes users’ OAuth tokens — Should Read

The Twitch Enhanced Viewer | JeetBot browser extension, installed by more than 30,000 users, exposes Twitch OAuth session tokens by forwarding them through JeetBot proxy servers in URL parameters. Users should remove the extension and revoke all Twitch sessions to invalidate potentially compromised tokens.

  • The Twitch Enhanced Viewer | JeetBot browser extension, available through the official Chrome and Firefox stores, has more than 30,000 installs.
  • Socket found that the extension captures Twitch web-client authorization information and sends users’ Twitch OAuth tokens through JeetBot-operated proxy servers.
  • The extension appends tokens to redirected proxy request URLs, causing the credentials to be recorded in proxy-server request logs in clear text.
  • Earlier versions explicitly transmitted users’ Twitch OAuth tokens to the developer’s server, according to a disclaimer in the Firefox Add-ons listing.
  • Socket recommends that users remove the extension, disconnect all Twitch sessions, and re-authenticate to invalidate tokens that may have been forwarded.

Red Heron Exploits Gitea RCE to Compromise 13 Organizations Across Six Countries — Must Read

China-linked Red Heron rapidly exploited the critical Gitea RCE CVE-2026-60004 to compromise 13 organizations across six countries, stealing source code and credentials and moving laterally into victim infrastructure. The campaign deployed the JITTERLY Linux backdoor and SIXZUT LD_PRELOAD rootkit for persistent, stealthy access.

  • Acronis attributed a multinational campaign to suspected China-linked actor Red Heron, which exploited the critical Gitea remote-code-execution flaw CVE-2026-60004 shortly after its July 2026 disclosure.
  • The campaign resulted in confirmed compromises of 13 organizations in Canada, Argentina, Taiwan, the United States, Qatar, and Sri Lanka, spanning sectors including defense, elections, energy, aerospace, telecommunications, government, public safety, and research.
  • Red Heron converted a public proof of concept into an automated Python framework that could register accounts, compromise vulnerable Gitea servers, steal repositories, and remove selected traces.
  • Researchers found the JITTERLY Linux implant, which supports more than 30 post-compromise functions, and the SIXZUT LD_PRELOAD rootkit, which hides files, processes, and network connections while helping the malware persist.
  • In one Taiwanese environment, the actor moved from a vulnerable Gitea server to root-level administrative access across a three-node Proxmox cluster.

New DDRop Attack Breaks Intel TDX and AMD SEV-SNP Confidential Computing — Should Read

Researchers demonstrated DDRop, a low-cost physical interposer attack that silently drops DDR5 memory writes and exploits missing freshness protections in Intel TDX, Scalable SGX, and AMD SEV-SNP. An attacker with server software control and brief physical access could undermine confidential-computing workloads, and fully addressing the flaw requires future hardware designs with memory freshness guarantees.

  • Researchers disclosed DDRop, a hardware attack that silently drops DDR5 memory writes so systems can read older encrypted data as though it were current.
  • DDRop requires an attacker to control server software and briefly access the machine to install an interposer between the processor and a memory module, with parts costing about $159.
  • The researchers demonstrated impacts on Intel TDX, Intel Scalable SGX, and AMD SEV-SNP; on Intel TDX, they showed victim-memory reading, debug-mode activation, and launch-measurement forgery under specified conditions.
  • AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud offer affected confidential-computing technologies, but the researchers said they have no evidence that DDRop or comparable active interposers have been used outside a laboratory.
  • The researchers said there is no simple patch because the flaw stems from hardware designs that lack memory freshness checks, while Intel and AMD characterize physical interposer attacks as outside their published threat models.

The group disputes Kaspersky’s attribution of the ransomware, highlighting the difficulty of tracking shared tools among Ukraine-linked hacktivist groups.

  • Hacking Cat has targeted Russian organizations since about February 2024 and shifted toward operations intended to encrypt and destroy data by summer 2025.

  • WordPress said the process detected a backdoor in a July 28, 2026 plugin release with about 20,000 active installations, and the compromised version was not distributed through the update API.

The sites collect contact and identity details, then scammers seek fees, financial information, or device access through malware disguised as verification apps.

Revolut handed customer data to fraudsters using government email account — Should Read

Revolut disclosed sensitive customer data after fraudsters used a legitimate government email domain to submit fraudulent emergency information requests, reportedly targeting high-net-worth crypto-linked users. Exposed information included identity documents, contact details, bank records, and transaction histories.

  • Revolut said an unauthorized party used a legitimate government agency email domain to submit fraudulent emergency requests for customer information.
  • The company said only a limited number of customers were affected, that it notified them directly, and that it blocked the email address after detecting the activity.
  • Affected customers' exposed information reportedly included dates of birth, contact details, passport and driver's license copies, verification selfies, bank statements, IBANs, withdrawal records, and transaction histories including Bitcoin activity.

Products: revolut

Your Own Mailing List Signed the Phishing Email — May Read

A phishing email authenticated by a legitimate external provider was accepted by an externally open Google Workspace accounting group, which redistributed and DKIM-signed it internally to four recipients. Restrict external posting to internal distribution groups and investigate cases where your own domain signs a message whose visible From address is external.

  • An externally authenticated phishing email was accepted by a regional equipment rental company’s Google Workspace accounting group and redistributed to four accounting mailboxes in the same second.
  • Google Groups rewrote the message envelope, applied a DKIM signature for the recipient company’s domain, added an ARC chain, and appended a list footer that caused its own DKIM signature to fail at delivery.
  • The email’s button redirected through a shared marketing-platform click tracker to a compromised WordPress administrative path on a real manufacturing business’s website.
  • The article states that neither the consumer ISP used for sending, the marketing click tracker, the recipient’s Google Workspace tenant, nor the compromised manufacturer website belonged to the attacker.
  • The recommended remediation is to restrict external posting to distribution groups that do not need to receive email from outside the organization.

Vendors: google, ironscales, wordpress

AI Changed the Exposure Problem. Validation Needs to Change With It. — Optional

AI is dramatically increasing vulnerability discovery, making CVSS-only prioritization inadequate; organizations need evidence-based validation of exploitability, control effectiveness, and attack paths to focus remediation on exposures that truly matter.

  • In the first half of 2026, 35,853 CVEs were published, roughly 49% more than in the previous year, while 495 were catalogued as exploited in the wild.
  • CVSS provides a common severity baseline but cannot determine whether a vulnerability is exploitable, reachable, or business-critical in a specific organization’s environment.
  • Omdia research found that 95% of organizations rank penetration testing as a top or high priority, but only 32% of their average attack surface is tested each year.
  • The article says automated penetration testing cannot validate every exposure because newly disclosed CVEs may lack a working exploit and live testing may be unsafe or impossible on critical, restricted, or air-gapped assets.
  • Picus argues that exploitability validation, security control validation, and agentic penetration testing should be combined to prioritize remediation and revalidate fixes.

CISA: Hackers now exploit max severity GitLab flaw in attacks — Must Read

CISA says attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-85706, a maximum-severity GitLab path traversal flaw that allows unauthenticated reading of sensitive files. Organizations should immediately upgrade GitLab CE/EE to versions 19.3.2, 19.2.6, or 19.1 and review logs for suspicious repository commits API requests.

  • CISA added CVE-2026-85706 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after hackers began exploiting the maximum-severity GitLab flaw.
  • The flaw affects GitLab's repository commits API and can let unauthenticated attackers read credentials, secrets, and other sensitive files from vulnerable servers.
  • GitLab fixed the issue in Community and Enterprise Edition versions 19.3.2, 19.2.6, and 19.1, and urged users to patch immediately.
  • watchTowr reported observing internet-wide probes for unpatched GitLab servers and advised defenders to review logs for suspicious POST requests to repository commits API URLs containing file.path parameters.
  • CISA gave U.S. federal agencies three days to secure affected systems under Binding Operational Directive 26-04 and encouraged all organizations to prioritize remediation.

Technologies: ci-cd, source-control

Products: gitlab-ce, gitlab-ee

Vendors: gitlab, watchtowr

Emerging Threat: (CVE-2026-78006) The Events Calendar Remote Code Execution via PHP Object Injection — Must Read

CVE-2026-78006 is a critical pre-authentication remote code execution flaw in The Events Calendar WordPress plugin affecting versions through 6.17.4, exploitable through comments enabled on event pages. Update to version 6.17.4.1 immediately and disable or restrict event comments until patching is verified.

  • CVE-2026-78006 is a critical PHP object injection flaw in StellarWP’s The Events Calendar WordPress plugin that can allow remote code execution on the underlying host.
  • The flaw can be exploited without an account or administrator interaction by submitting malicious comment content to an event page, provided comments are enabled and visible.
  • All The Events Calendar versions through 6.17.4 are affected, while version 6.17.4.1, released on September 10, 2026, fixes the issue.
  • Organizations should inventory public WordPress sites, including agency-managed, acquired, staging, and pre-production properties, because calendar sites are often outside central IT patching processes.
  • Until patching is confirmed, organizations should disable event comments where unnecessary or require commenters to authenticate.

Vendors: stellarwp, wordfence, cycognito

Microsoft: September updates cause RDS failures on Windows Server — Should Read

Microsoft confirmed that September 2026 security updates can destabilize Remote Desktop Services on Windows Server 2012 and later, causing failed RDP connections, sign-in problems, and server hangs. Administrators can deploy Microsoft’s Known Issue Rollback Group Policy as a temporary mitigation while a permanent fix is developed.

  • Microsoft confirmed that September 2026 security updates can make Remote Desktop Services unstable on Windows Server 2012 and later, as well as Windows 10 and Windows 11 devices.
  • Affected systems may experience failed remote connections after several minutes, sign-in problems, servers hanging during remote-desktop configuration, and unresponsive management tools or Windows Update pages.
  • Existing remote sessions may fail to disconnect or log off properly, while new connection attempts can hang and fail.
  • Microsoft has released version-specific Group Policy Known Issue Rollback packages to mitigate the issue on enterprise-managed devices.
  • Restarting an affected virtual machine may temporarily restore remote access, while uninstalling the problematic updates can restore functionality but removes that month’s security fixes.

Malicious Twitch Browser Extension Leaks OAuth Tokens From Nearly 31,000 Users — Should Read

The Twitch Enhanced Viewer | JeetBot browser extension exposed OAuth session tokens from nearly 31,000 Chrome and Firefox users by sending them to operator-controlled proxy servers, potentially enabling account actions such as reading whispers, chatting, and spending channel points. Users should disable or update the extension immediately and revoke affected Twitch sessions, since updating does not invalidate tokens already transmitted.

  • The Twitch Enhanced Viewer | JeetBot extension on the Chrome Web Store and Firefox Add-Ons store exposed OAuth tokens associated with nearly 31,000 users by forwarding them to operator-controlled proxy servers.
  • The extension sent users' Twitch tokens as an auth query parameter when routing video-playlist requests through its proxy infrastructure, causing the tokens to be recorded in proxy request logs in cleartext.
  • A Twitch OAuth session token can allow its holder to act on an account without its password or second factor, including reading and sending whispers, posting in chat, and spending channel points.
  • The token-forwarding behavior excluded a hard-coded list of 10 Twitch channels, most of which are Russian-language streamers.
  • JeetBot's documentation says Firefox extension version 85.8.7 no longer sends users' Twitch OAuth tokens to its proxies, but tokens transmitted by older versions are not revoked by updating or disabling the extension.

Technologies: browser, proxy, iam

Products: twitch-enhanced-viewer-jeetbot, jeetbot, twitch, google-chrome-web-store, firefox-add-ons

Vendors: jeetbot, twitch, google, mozilla, socket

Revolut disclosed that attackers impersonating a government agency used an unauthorized but domain-authenticated email account to obtain highly sensitive data from a limited number of customers, including identity documents, selfies, account statements, and transaction histories. The company says its systems and customer funds were not affected.

  • Revolut disclosed that it shared customer data with a threat actor who impersonated a government agency through an unauthorized email account using the agency’s official email domain.
  • The exposed data included identity and contact details, passport or driver’s license copies, facial verification images, account statements with IBAN numbers, withdrawal records, and complete transaction histories including Bitcoin transactions.
  • Revolut said the breach affected a very limited but undisclosed number of customers and that its systems and customer funds were unaffected.
  • Revolut said it blocked the email address after detecting the incident and notified the relevant government agency, law enforcement, data-protection authorities, and financial regulators.

Microsoft confirmed that September 2026 Windows 11 security updates KB5124008 and KB5124012 can prevent some USB Audio Class 1.0 devices from starting or producing sound, particularly in multichannel modes.   • The issue affects only systems running Windows 11 version 24H2 or later and is limited to USB Audio Class 1.0 devices.
  • Affected users reported Device Manager Code 10 errors, no audio output, and unresponsive volume controls and sound settings.
  • Some impacted USB audio speakers fail only when multichannel features such as 3D audio or 8-channel modes are used.
  • Microsoft has not provided an official workaround, but some users restored audio by switching to 2-channel mode.

Products: windows-11, windows-11-24h2, windows-11-25h2, dirac-audio, intel-smart-sound-technology

Vendors: microsoft, dirac, intel

How the UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill Extends to the Supply Chain — Optional

The UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill could extend cyber-security obligations beyond critical infrastructure operators to their suppliers, through formal critical-supplier designations and tougher contractual requirements. Manufacturers and OT technology providers should prepare to demonstrate their product security posture and supply-chain risk management before customers demand it.

  • The UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill directly regulates Operators of Essential Services, managed service providers, and data centre operators.
  • The Bill proposes a Designated Critical Supplier category that would allow regulators to impose equivalent security, incident-reporting, inspection, and turnover-based penalty obligations on designated suppliers.
  • Organisations regulated under the Bill are likely to pass security expectations to suppliers through procurement requirements, due-diligence requests, and contractual audit rights.
  • Manufacturers and technology providers supplying regulated sectors may need to demonstrate details of their products' security posture, including known weaknesses, network behaviour, update mechanisms, and required access.
  • The article states that manufacturers should understand both which regulated sectors their products reach and the cyber risks posed by their own suppliers and connected plant-network technology.

CyCognito has launched a beta MCP server that lets AI clients such as Claude, Cursor, and ChatGPT query its external attack-surface and exposure data using CyQL. The read-only integration preserves existing user permissions and supports asset, issue, evidence, and archived-issue searches.

Thorough reorganization at NSA will create five 'mission centers,' including cyber and AI — Should Read

The NSA is rapidly reorganizing into five mission centers focused on China, cybersecurity, AI, combat support, and global intelligence to move intelligence to military users faster. The overhaul, targeted for full capability by January, leaves key details unresolved and risks repeating problems from past restructurings.

  • The National Security Agency is replacing its existing directorates with five mission centers focused on China, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, combat support, and global intelligence.
  • NSA Director and U.S. Cyber Command head Army Gen. Joshua Rudd informed the workforce of the changes and began a 30-day implementation period.
  • The new mission centers are expected to reach full operational capability by January, according to a former NSA official.
  • The placement of some organizations, including the Cybersecurity Collaboration Center, remains unclear, while Tailored Access Operations is expected to fall under global intelligence.
  • Current and former officials said agency leaders expect the rapid reorganization to disrupt parts of the NSA bureaucracy and require adjustments during implementation.

item.title: UNC3569 Exploits CVE-2026-51990 in Tencent Sogou to Deploy GrayRabbit
item.content:encoded:
Window: 13 Sep 14:00 → 13 Sep 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hackers exploit Tencent app flaw to deploy GrayRabbit malware — Must Read

China-linked UNC3569 is actively exploiting CVE-2026-51990 in Tencent Sogou Input Method for Windows to deploy the GrayRabbit backdoor through a one-click crafted link. Tencent patched the protocol-handler flaw in version 16.3.0.3498, but the app’s outdated, unsandboxed Chromium engine remains a security concern.

  • Gen Threat Labs reported that UNC3569 is actively exploiting CVE-2026-51990 in Tencent’s Sogou Input Method for Windows to deploy the GrayRabbit backdoor through crafted links.
  • The one-click attack abuses Sogou’s sgbiz: link handler to pass attacker-controlled instructions to the application, which then opens an attacker-controlled web page in its embedded browser.
  • The malicious page exploits a known flaw in Sogou’s outdated Chromium 80 browser engine, which runs without a sandbox and with key web protections disabled, to execute code and install GrayRabbit.
  • GrayRabbit can run programs, provide interactive remote command access, transfer files, collect system and user information, and load additional components into memory.
  • Tencent released Sogou Input Method version 16.3.0.3498 on April 21 to restrict protocol-handler URLs, though researchers warned that its underlying browser remains outdated and unsandboxed.

Products: sogou-input-method, chromium
